subject: Invoice routing: marketplace vs vendor invoice for procurement
messages:
From: Alex Tan <procurement@finedge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Cara Nguyen <cfo@finedge.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement question — marketplace vs vendor invoice

Hi Olga,

We're nearing internal approvals for the pilot (DEAL-8721) and our procurement team asked a practical question: would you recommend we buy through AWS Marketplace (so AWS invoices us) or sign a direct vendor invoice with Redwood?

Key constraints for us:
- We need Net 45 payment terms if possible.
- Our AP team prefers a single-vendor bill on our Oracle system.
- We may want to take advantage of co-sell credits if available.

Can you outline trade-offs (timing for PO, invoicing cadence, any co-sell/rebate implications, and typical tax/withholding differences) so we can present to finance? I attached a draft SOW for context.

Thanks,
Alex Tan
Procurement Manager
FinEdge Corp
Attachment: Finedge_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tan <procurement@finedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace vs vendor invoice

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: both routes are possible; the right choice depends on what you prioritize. Below is a short comparison and recommended next steps for FinEdge.

Marketplace (AWS / Azure / GCP):
- Timing: Fastest to provision once the listing is in place — typically 3–7 business days for a standard SaaS listing to be accepted and mapping to your account.
- Invoicing: AWS invoices your company; Redwood receives payment from AWS. That means your AP team will see a single line item from AWS.
- Payment terms: Marketplace invoices are usually standard AWS terms (Net 30 by default); extending to Net 45 requires coordination with your AWS account team and may not be guaranteed.
- Co-sell: If you want AWS co-sell credits, you need the marketplace listing plus the appropriate co-sell registration (we can coordinate). Credits usually apply to recognized bookings but timing to realize credits can lag.
- Tax/withholding: Marketplace often handles tax collection differently — AWS may collect VAT/sales tax in some regions; US corporate withholding is not typical.

Direct vendor invoice (Redwood issues invoice):
- Timing: Can be as fast as same-day to a few days after PO acceptance — we can issue a vendor invoice on receipt of your PO.
- Invoicing: Invoice lands directly from Redwood which fits your single-vendor preference and Oracle reconciliation.
- Payment terms: More flexibility — we can entertain Net 45 on contracted deals (requires approval from our finance lead).
- Co-sell: Direct invoice can still be part of co-sell but you may miss marketplace-native incentives unless we coordinate an equivalent channel rebate.
- Tax/withholding: Standard vendor invoicing processes; any US withholding would be handled per the vendor terms.

Recommendation for FinEdge:
1) If AP system/PO timing is the blocker and Net 45 is a hard requirement, take the direct vendor invoice path — we can issue Redwood invoice and accept Net 45 upon finance approval (I can loop in finance).
2) If you prefer minimal vendor management and want to capture AWS co-sell benefits, go marketplace — note this may impose Net 30 and a short delay to realize co-sell credits.

Next steps I can take immediately:
- Loop in our finance lead (Rishi) to confirm whether Net 45 is approvable for DEAL-8721.
- Share the marketplace listing terms and expected timeline.
- If you prefer vendor invoice, send PO format and we’ll prepare an invoice and SOW signature package.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0190

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tan <procurement@finedge.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace vs vendor invoice

Alex — adding a few channel specifics from partnerships/finance perspective:

1) Marketplace listing items to watch:
- Listing acceptance: AWS will want legal/contact info and a technical listing manifest. We already have a pre-approved Redwood listing; I can submit a private offer for FinEdge which shortens acceptance.
- Private offers: If you want Net 45, we can request a private offer via AWS. Private offer terms are negotiable between AWS/Redwood and you — timeline varies but often 1–2 weeks once Azure/AWS reps engage.

2) Co-sell & incentives:
- AWS co-sell credits are applied to the partner (Redwood) and passed as discounts; from your POV the purchase route (marketplace vs direct) can affect how credits are processed. If you need those incentives immediately reflected on your invoice, we should coordinate a private offer or apply a vendor-level rebate (we can document in the SOW).

3) Reconciliation and PO fields:
- If you plan to use Oracle, please include our Redwood vendor name exactly as: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Typical required PO fields for vendor invoice: remit-to address, tax ID, contact person, and invoice reference. (I’ve attached a vendor-bill workbook that our finance team fills to speed processing.)

I’ll help push a private offer path with AWS if that’s preferred — that preserves marketplace benefits while allowing negotiable payment terms.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Vendor-Bill-Workbook.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alex Tan <procurement@finedge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Cara Nguyen <cfo@finedge.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace vs vendor invoice

Thanks both — this is exactly what finance needed. Quick answers:
- FinEdge prefers to preserve potential AWS incentives but Net 45 is a hard requirement for our AP cycle.
- We’re happy to accept a private offer if Redwood/AWS can create one that allows Net 45 and shows the co-sell credit flow (even if credits post-facto).

Next actions from our side:
1) I’ll route an internal PO template to Laura (attached) and request our AWS account team to approve private offer slack channel.
2) Please have Rishi confirm Redwood’s ability to accept Net 45 on a private-offer backed purchase and the invoice flow for accounting.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we aim to get PO over by next Tuesday.

Best,
Alex Tan
Procurement Manager
FinEdge Corp
Attachment: FinEdge_PO_Template.xlsx (xlsx)
